facts.source_title: White label web analytics for SaaS platforms and website builders | Plausible Analytics

facts.source_title: Plausible Analytics | Simple, privacy-friendly Google Analytics alternative

facts.excerpt: Plausible crossed $1 million in annual recurring revenue in 2022 and has continued to grow as a profitable, independently operated company.

facts.claim: Plausible says its analytics do not use cookies or collect personal data.

strategy.observation: Plausible says it has never spent on advertising and has grown through recommendations.
strategy.offer_link: Paid search could be a limited way to test whether people actively searching for privacy-focused analytics convert, without assuming Plausible should replace its recommendation-led growth.
hypotheses: Plausible may be open to testing an additional acquisition channel.
There may be enough high-intent search demand for privacy-focused analytics to justify a small campaign.
strategy.angle: Since Plausible says it has never spent on advertising and has grown through recommendations, would you consider testing paid search for people actively looking for privacy-focused analytics?
strategy.fit_reason: The offer is relevant to a privacy-focused software product, but Plausible has explicitly grown without advertising, so paid search may not align with its established acquisition approach or current priorities.

draft.subject: A small paid search test
draft.body:
Plausible says it has never spent on advertising and has grown through recommendations. A small paid search test could add a channel alongside that approach, focused on people actively searching for privacy-focused analytics.

I run paid search campaigns for privacy-focused software products. The point would be to see whether those high-intent searches convert, not to replace recommendation-led growth.

Would you consider a limited test on a few privacy-focused analytics searches?

draft.subject: A small paid search test
draft.body:
Plausible says it has never spent on advertising and has grown through recommendations. Paid search could be a small way to see whether people actively searching for privacy-focused analytics convert, without changing that approach.

I run paid search campaigns for privacy-focused software products. Would you consider testing a limited campaign against a few high-intent searches for privacy-focused analytics?

issues: “without changing that approach” implies paid search would not change Plausible’s recommendation-led approach, but paid advertising would be a change. Rephrase to make clear it would be a small test alongside its existing approach.
